Derived, not captured: `exec_long_commandline.ndjson` is the `/bin/ls` exec of `../esf/exec.json` re-pointed at `/usr/bin/curl` with its args extended to 412 characters (`https://` at 382); `alf_firewall_disabled.ndjson` is the first line of `../ul/com_apple_ALF_ApplicationFirewall.ndjson` with its eventMessage set to a sentence containing "Firewall disabled".

Synthetic, from Apple's headers (no capture has these events): `xp_malware.ndjson` (an `xp_malware_detected` and an `xp_malware_remediated`) and `gatekeeper_user_override.ndjson` (one override whose `file` is an `es_file_t`, one whose `file` is the bare path string ESF reports when it can't resolve the file). Each is the first line of `../esf/profile_add.json` with its `event_type` and `event` replaced. The event bodies use the member names of `es_event_xp_malware_detected_t`, `es_event_xp_malware_remediated_t` and `es_event_gatekeeper_user_override_t` in `EndpointSecurity/ESMessage.h` (macOS 27.2 SDK), as eslogger names keys after struct members; the values are made up. The bare-path `file` follows eslogger's other unions with a string arm (an OD `member_value` is the name itself): `eslogger` has no `file_path` key.
